# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** Christ's conception was not by a man. By "biological father" I mean the man whose seed begets the child. The KJV names one source for the conception, the Holy Ghost, and it names a woman who "know[s] not a man." Joseph is Mary's husband and the child's guardian, but he is not the one who begot him.

---

## 1. The conception took place before any union

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] The Greek *prin ē synelthein autous* means "before they came together." *Synerchomai* (G4905) means to come together. The text sets the conception before the union. The phrase *ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of the Holy Ghost." *Ek* (G1537) marks source or origin.

[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The word "till" carries the non-union through the whole pregnancy to the birth.

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the union, and Matthew 1:25 keeps the union from happening until after the birth. The only source named for the pregnancy is *ek pneumatos hagiou*. So no union with Joseph (or any man) lies behind the conception.

## 2. The angel names the source

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] *To en autē gennēthen* means "that which is begotten in her." *Gennaō* (G1080) is the verb used of a father begetting and of a mother bearing. The origin is again *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Ghost." The "for" (*gar*) gives the reason Joseph should not fear. Joseph's fear is about the child's origin, and the answer is the Holy Ghost.

[L3] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] *Epeleusetai* means "shall come upon." *Episkiasei* means "shall overshadow." The "therefore" (*dio*) makes the conception by the Holy Ghost the reason the child is called the Son of God.

[L4] Footing: Matthew 1:20 names the source of the begetting (*ek*), and Luke 1:35 names the agent and the result. Both texts name the Holy Ghost as the one acting. Neither gives a place to a man's seed. [L3] Hebrews 10:5 says, "a body hast thou prepared me." The Greek *katartizō* (G2675) means to fit or prepare. The body is described as prepared by God.

## 3. Mary's own testimony

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097), "to know," is used here of sexual relations. The Hebrew *yāda'* (H3045) is used the same way. [L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain."

[L4] Footing: Luke 1:34 uses "know" in the sense Genesis 4:1 shows, where "knew" leads to "conceived." Mary says she has not known a man. The answer she receives in Luke 1:35 gives the Holy Ghost as the way it will be, and does not point to a man. [L3] Luke 1:27 calls her "a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph." Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."

## 4. Joseph is not the one who begat

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] Every earlier line in the genealogy uses *egennēsen* (G1080), "begat," with a man as subject. In verse 16 the pattern changes. The relative *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular. *Egennēthē* is passive, "was born." Joseph is called *anēr* (G435), "husband," of Mary. The text does not say "Joseph begat Jesus."

[L3] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." [L2] *Dikaios* (G1342) means righteous or just. [L4] Footing: Joseph is called just in Matthew 1:19, and in Matthew 1:20 the angel reassures him about taking Mary, which shows he did not take himself to be the father. His intent to put her away fits a man who knows the child is not his.

[L3] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph." [L2] *Enomizeto* (G3543) means "was thought" or "was reckoned." The KJV marks Joseph's fatherhood as the supposition of others. [L3] Luke 2:48–49: Mary says "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." The child answers, "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" The child does not accept Joseph as the father in that sense.

## 5. The sign

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

[L2] The Hebrew is *'almāh* (H5959), the word the KJV renders "virgin." [L3] Genesis 24:43 uses *'almāh* of Rebekah, and Genesis 24:16 describes her as "a virgin, neither had any man known her."

[L1] Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet… Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son." [L2] Matthew's Greek is *parthenos* (G3933), "virgin."

[L4] Footing: Isaiah 7:14 calls the conception a "sign" from the Lord. Matthew 1:22–23 ties the fulfilment to Mary with the word "virgin." A conception by a man would not be a sign.

## 6. What the supposed father texts do and do not show

[L1] Luke 4:22: "Is not this Joseph's son?" [L1] John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." These are the speech of the crowd and of Philip. [L3] Luke 3:23 marks that belief as "as was supposed," and Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35 give the truth about the source.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." [L3] Luke 1:31–32: the child is conceived in Mary's womb and receives "the throne of his father David." [L3] Matthew 1:20–21, 25: Joseph, "son of David," takes Mary as his wife and names the child, so the child is reckoned in his house. [L4] Footing: Luke 1:31–32 ties David's promise to the child born of Mary, and Matthew 1:20–25 shows Joseph's role as receiving and naming. Neither requires Joseph's seed. The "flesh" of Romans 1:3 is the body born of the woman (Luke 1:35, "born of thee").

**Position.** The child was "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). The seed came "out of" the loins of David's line, and the line is reckoned "by the house of their fathers" (Numbers 1:2). The one man the text names in that house is Joseph. He is Mary's husband from the espousal, and the text calls him the child's father in four voices.
